textData.text: Burning, tingling, numbness and radiating pain can make everyday tasks difficult. They can also arise for different reasons. Finding the cause is the first step; a wellness service should not be presented as a diagnosis or a cure for nerve damage.

This anatomical illustration highlights the sciatic nerve pathway and lumbar spine inflammation, a common source of nerve pain. It visually represents sciatica and the potential benefits of therapies like massage and red light treatment, which target inflammation and nerve compression at the source.

imageData.altText: Illustration of the lower spine and sciatic nerve with a highlighted area of discomfort
imageData.caption: Illustration of the lower spine and sciatic nerve. This is educational imagery, not a depiction of a treatment outcome.

textData.text: Begin with medical guidance

Discuss new, persistent or worsening nerve symptoms with a healthcare professional. Ask which activities and types of touch are appropriate, whether there are areas to avoid and what changes should prompt further assessment. Bring those instructions to a bodywork appointment.
What massage may offer

When appropriate for your condition, massage can focus on comfort, relaxation and surrounding muscle tension. A chronic low-back pain trial reported benefits for symptoms and function, but that finding does not demonstrate nerve regrowth or apply to every neuropathy or sciatica diagnosis.
Reduced discomfort during a session should not be interpreted as proof that damaged nerves have healed. The goal and the way progress is assessed should be clear from the start.
Pressure and technique should fit the person
More pressure is not automatically more useful. Tell your therapist about reduced sensation and any area where feedback may be unreliable.
Deep tissue massage
and
manual lymphatic drainage
are different services; neither should be selected solely because the word “nerve” appears in a symptom description.
Where red light fits
You can read about
red light therapy at Matrix

to understand the wellness service. This article does not establish a panel protocol that remyelinates nerves, restores lost sensation or treats neuropathy. A fixed series of appointments should not be sold on those promises.
Supplements need an individual reason

B12 deficiency can affect nerve function, while excess supplemental B6 can cause nerve problems. That makes individualized assessment more useful than a standard combination of B vitamins, alpha-lipoic acid and other products. Review supplements and doses with your clinician or pharmacist.
Our
supplement page
provides access information; it is not a substitute for that assessment.

Explore our
massage therapy services
and describe your goals and relevant medical instructions before booking. We can discuss whether a comfort-focused appointment is appropriate without promising a medical outcome.
View available appointments
for current service options. The right next step is a clear plan that respects both your wellness preferences and your ongoing care.
Research and references
Cherkin et al. — chronic low-back pain massage trial (2011)
NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — vitamin B12
NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — vitamin B6

textData.text: A good massage starts with a useful goal. You may want a quiet hour, attention to tense shoulders or a comfortable way to care for muscles after a demanding week. Research can help frame those choices without turning every session into a promise of a medical result.
Relaxation and stress
Massage Appointments Salem / Paddock Lake, WI

imageData.altText: Woman receiving a massage in Salem, WI on a bed in a serene room, blue art on walls. Text: "De-Stress & Unwind," "Matrix Massage & Bodywork," contact info.
imageData.caption: Massage Appointments Salem / Paddock Lake, WI

textData.text: Massage gives you time to pause and communicate what feels comfortable. Small clinical studies have explored anxiety-related outcomes, but their results should not be stretched into a guarantee that massage corrects hormones or replaces mental-health care.
Muscle comfort and pain
Pain Relieving Massage at Matrix Massage in Salem / Paddock Lake, WI

imageData.altText: Illustration of a massage session in a softly lit room
imageData.caption: Massage and muscle comfort

textData.text: A randomized trial in adults with nonspecific chronic low-back pain found improvements in symptoms and function after a course of massage. That supports a focused discussion about certain pain concerns; it does not establish that massage treats every cause of pain.
Tell your therapist where you feel discomfort, which activities bother you and what healthcare guidance you have received. Pressure and positioning can then be selected around a meaningful goal.
Recovery after activity
Boost Athletic Recovery with Deep Tissue Massage in Salem, WI

imageData.altText: Illustration of a person resting on a gym floor
imageData.caption: Making time for rest after activity

textData.text: Some small studies have examined post-exercise soreness. Feeling less sore is different from proving faster tissue repair or better athletic performance. Massage also should not be explained as flushing out lactic acid.
What about immunity?

Research measuring short-term immune markers is not the same as research showing fewer infections. We therefore describe massage around comfort and relaxation rather than claiming it boosts protection against illness.
Make the appointment useful to you

Before your visit, choose one or two priorities. During the session, speak up about temperature, pressure and positioning. Afterward, notice comfort and everyday function rather than expecting a specific laboratory or hormone change. Discuss persistent symptoms with your healthcare professional.

Union Grove
, explore the local service information and plan travel around your starting point.
View massage appointments in Salem
to find the current options and choose a session that fits your goals.
Research and references
Rapaport et al. — preliminary massage biomarker study (2010)
Cherkin et al. — chronic low-back pain massage trial (2011)
Rapaport et al. — massage and anxiety proof-of-concept trial (2016)
Hilbert et al. — massage and delayed muscle soreness (2003)
Wiltshire et al. — massage and lactate removal (2010)

textData.text: Numbers such as 660 or 850 describe a wavelength in nanometers, often abbreviated nm. They tell you something about the light a device emits. They do not, on their own, tell you whether a session is right for your goal or how much benefit to expect.
NIR & red light therapy panel emitting 660nm and 850nm wavelengths for skin, muscle, and cellular healing benefits

imageData.altText: Person resting beneath a curved red light device
imageData.caption: A red light session. Equipment specifications and instructions depend on the device.

textData.text: Red and near-infrared

Red light is visible. Near-infrared light lies outside the visible red range. Products may use one region or a combination. That does not create a simple rule that one wavelength treats skin while another automatically treats nerves, joints or the brain.
Wavelength is one part of the treatment

Output, exposure area, distance and session time also affect delivery. A study using a directed laser is not automatically a study of a broad LED panel, even if a wavelength number looks similar. Device instructions and the evidence for the intended use matter together.
What research helps explain

Some controlled skin research has reported improvements in appearance. Exercise studies have explored particular doses and outcomes. These are useful research areas, but neither gives a universal distance-and-time chart for every consumer device.
Questions worth asking

What equipment will be used? What is the session intended to offer? Which instructions apply to eye protection, positioning and exposure? Is the claim based on research using comparable equipment, or only on a matching wavelength label?

Be cautious about exact tissue-depth promises or claims that adding more wavelengths makes a treatment universally stronger. The numbers are a starting point for understanding the equipment, not a diagnosis or a treatment prescription.
Choosing a Matrix session

Use the current service description to understand the experience offered, and discuss relevant medical precautions before your visit. Follow the instructions for the equipment being used rather than applying a protocol from a different device.
Explore
red light therapy in Salem
for Matrix’s current service information and appointment options.
Research and references
Wunsch and Matuschka — controlled skin light study (2014)
Vanin et al. — exercise photobiomodulation trial (2016)
